metadata.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate (Bahdanau, Cho, Bengio, 2014)
metadata.framework: attention mechanism for sequence-to-sequence neural machine translation
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1409.0473.

nodes.name: Encoder-decoder architecture for NMT
nodes.statement: A neural machine translation model encodes a source sentence $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \ldots, x_{T_x})$ into a sequence of hidden states, and a decoder generates the target sentence $\mathbf{y} = (y_1, \ldots, y_{T_y})$ one token at a time, conditioned on the encoding and previously generated tokens: $p(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}) = \prod_{t=1}^{T_y} p(y_t | y_{<t}, \mathbf{x})$.

nodes.name: Bidirectional RNN encoder
nodes.statement: The encoder is a bidirectional RNN. The forward RNN reads $x_1, \ldots, x_{T_x}$ producing $\overrightarrow{h}_1, \ldots, \overrightarrow{h}_{T_x}$; the backward RNN reads $x_{T_x}, \ldots, x_1$ producing $\overleftarrow{h}_1, \ldots, \overleftarrow{h}_{T_x}$. The annotation of each word is $h_j = [\overrightarrow{h}_j; \overleftarrow{h}_j]$ (concatenation), capturing context from both directions.

nodes.name: Attention mechanism (additive attention)
nodes.statement: At each decoder step $i$, compute attention scores over encoder annotations: $e_{ij} = a(s_{i-1}, h_j)$ where $a$ is an alignment model (feedforward network): $a(s, h) = \mathbf{v}_a^\top \tanh(W_a s + U_a h)$. Attention weights: $\alpha_{ij} = \frac{\exp(e_{ij})}{\sum_{k=1}^{T_x} \exp(e_{ik})}$ (softmax over source positions). Context vector: $c_i = \sum_{j=1}^{T_x} \alpha_{ij} h_j$.

nodes.name: Attention-based decoder
nodes.statement: The decoder is a GRU-based RNN where the conditional probability of each target word depends on the previous hidden state $s_{i-1}$, the previous target word $y_{i-1}$, and the attention context vector $c_i$: $p(y_i | y_{<i}, \mathbf{x}) = g(y_{i-1}, s_i, c_i)$ where $s_i = f(s_{i-1}, y_{i-1}, c_i)$ and $g$ is a softmax over the vocabulary.

nodes.name: Soft alignment as attention
nodes.statement: The attention weights $\alpha_{ij}$ define a soft alignment between target position $i$ and source positions $j$. Unlike hard alignment in statistical MT, this soft alignment is differentiable and learned jointly with the translation model. The model 'jointly learns to align and translate'.

nodes.name: Attention solves the bottleneck problem
nodes.statement: Without attention, the encoder must compress the entire source sentence into a fixed-length context vector $c$, creating an information bottleneck especially for long sentences. With attention, the decoder can access any encoder hidden state via the weighted sum $c_i$, eliminating the bottleneck. Empirically, BLEU score degradation on long sentences is significantly reduced.
conclusions: No information bottleneck for long sentences
Significant BLEU improvement on sentences > 20 tokens

nodes.name: English-French translation results
nodes.statement: On WMT'14 English-to-French, the attention model achieves 36.15 BLEU (comparable to phrase-based SMT) and degrades much less on long sentences than the basic encoder-decoder (Cho et al. 2014). Attention alignments visualized as heatmaps show meaningful correspondence between source and target words.
